content.text: The naive induction on `xs` won't work, because `weave (x :: xs) ys` recurses on `weave ys xs` with the lists swapped. I'll prove a stronger statement by induction on the total length, covering both the equal-length case and the case where the first list is one longer.

have key : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ xs ys : List α, xs.length + ys.length ≤ n →
      (xs.length = ys.length ∨ xs.length = ys.length + 1) →
      deal (weave xs ys) = (xs, ys) := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero =>
      intro xs ys hn _
      have hx : xs = [] := List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega)
      have hy : ys = [] := List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega)
      subst hx; subst hy
      rfl
    | succ n ih =>
      intro xs ys hn hor
      cases xs with
      | nil =>
        cases ys with
        | nil => rfl
        | cons y ys => simp only [List.length_nil, List.length_cons] at hor; omega
      | cons x xs' =>
        cases ys with
        | nil => simp only [List.length_nil, List.length_cons] at hor; omega
        | cons y ys' =>
          have hor' : (y :: ys').length = xs'.length ∨ (y :: ys').length = xs'.length + 1 := by
            simp only [List.length_cons] at hor ⊢; omega
          have hn' : (y :: ys').length + xs'.length ≤ n := by
            simp only [List.length_cons] at hn ⊢; omega
          have h1 := ih (y :: ys') xs' hn' hor'
          rw [weave, deal, h1]
  exact key (xs.length + ys.length) xs ys le_rfl (Or.inl h)
